title: Smoke Test — Event Reconciliation dashboard (side-by-side layout + money-bearing scope fix)
subtitle: Re-validates the reconciliation widget after two changes: the two cards now sit side by side in a flex row (961d86aa), and reconciliation scope was widened so an order that moved money still counts even when CANCELLED (63788383) — so the breakdown ties to the processor's own gross/refund/net.

meta.Flow: Login → event 328 dashboard → Event Reconciliation + Funds by Channel cards → edit + save a Stripe channel fee
meta.Layout change: 961d86aa — Reconciliation and Funds-by-Channel wrapped in a flex row (channel table gets more room); stacks below the md breakpoint
meta.Scope fix: 63788383 — orders count if an active/expected sale OR they actually moved money (kept/refunded Stripe charge, or ledger rows); RESERVED/ABANDONED still drop out
meta.Event: 328 (smoke:reversal-fixture) enriched with an 8-order ledger: every transaction_type x payment_method axis PLUS a CANCELLED Stripe order whose $100 charge was kept and $40 refunded
meta.Service check: EventReconciliationService::reconcile(328) printed gross=551.57 refunds=60 comps=25 write_offs=10 donations=25 net_expected=481.57 collected=480 — matches the cards exactly

steps.title: Event dashboard loads
steps.description: Event 328 dashboard top — existing stat boxes and the sales chart are unaffected; the reconciliation cards are appended below them.

steps.title: Two cards now sit side by side
steps.description: The new flex row: Event Reconciliation on the left, the wider Funds by Channel table on the right. The whole story reads in one viewport — waterfall on the left ties to the per-channel breakdown on the right.
steps.notes: Below the md breakpoint these stack vertically (not captured here). This side-by-side arrangement is the layout change in 961d86aa.

steps.title: Reconciliation card — waterfall ties out
steps.description: Three tiles (Net expected $481.57, Collected $480.00 @ 100%, Net to bank $480.00) over the waterfall: Gross $551.57 − Refunds $60.00 − Comps (forgiven) $35.00 + Donations $25.00 = Net expected $481.57.
steps.notes: Comps (forgiven) $35.00 merges COMP ($25) + WRITE_OFF ($10). Gross $551.57 = the seeded $550 of in-scope orders plus the fixture's untouched $1.57 awaiting-payment order (the $1.57 uncollected gap rounds the progress bar to 100%). The $551.57 gross now INCLUDES the cancelled order's $100 — netted back out by the refunds line — which is exactly the 63788383 scope fix.

steps.title: Funds by Channel — cancelled-but-paid Stripe order reconciles
steps.description: Per-channel rows: Stripe $300.00 sales / − / −$40.00 refund, Square $100.00 / $10.00 / −$20.00, Cash $50.00 / $15.00, Check $40.00, Bank transfer $25.00. Totals $515.00 sales / $25.00 donations / −$60.00 refunds / 100%.
steps.notes: KEY VALIDATION of 63788383: Stripe $300 = $200 from a COMPLETED order + $100 from a CANCELLED order whose charge was kept; its $40 refund is the Stripe −$40.00. Under the old COMPLETED/AWAITING-only scope that order vanished entirely and Stripe would read $200 with no refund — failing to tie to the processor. PAYMENT rows -> sales, DONATION rows -> donations, COMP+WRITE_OFF -> the footer ($25 comps · $10 write-offs). Cash & Check fee inputs are disabled (no processing fee); Stripe, Square, Bank transfer are editable.

steps.title: Edit a channel fee (dirty state)
steps.description: Setting the Stripe fee from $0.00 to $7.50 enables the 'Save fees' button.

steps.title: Save fee — persisted, recorded & recomputed
steps.description: Save fires the PATCH and recomputes across both cards: Stripe fee $7.50 -> Totals fee $7.50, the waterfall's Processing fees line -> −$7.50, Net to bank (est.) -> $472.50. Footer stamps 'Fees updated May 31, 2026' and the Save button returns to disabled.
steps.notes: DB confirms the round-trip: event_channel_fees upserted all five channels, STRIPE fee_amount=7.50, recorded_by_user_id=546. Full edit -> persist -> reconcile -> re-render cycle works, and the recomputed total flows into the left card's waterfall, not just the right card's table.
